proof_summary: Define the candidate linear-recurrence sequence \(L_0=4,L_1=16,L_2=63\), \(L_{n+3}=4L_{n+2}-L_n\), and its defect \(D_n=L_{n+1}^2-L_{n+2}L_n\); algebra shows \(D_0,D_1,D_2=(4,1,16)\) and \(D_{n+3}=4D_{n+1}+D_n\). Induction using the growth bound \(L_{n+1}\ge3L_n\) gives \(1\le D_n\le L_n\), which makes \(\lceil L_{n+1}^2/L_n\rceil-1=L_{n+2}\), so the nonlinear original rule coincides with the claimed linear recurrence.
